bluf: Hook Agency is a Minneapolis agency selling SEO and PPC lead generation to roofing, HVAC, plumbing, remodeling, construction and storage contractors. It is doing self promotion and AI search content: Inc. 5000 listings in 2025 and 2026, 32 of its own Google ads, and 12 blog URLs on GEO, AEO and ChatGPT visibility with no named AI service captured. Horus reads it Neutral at +7, best placed for KJ1 and most exposed to KJ4; Monsoon reads Landfall at 75.0 with displacement at 81.0. A rival should know: the book is 4 names with no described work and the sitemap shows nothing updated in 90 days.
doing:
The positioning line, a Minneapolis agency for roofers, HVAC, plumbing, remodeling and construction contractors selling SEO and PPC lead generation built on home services expertise, decodes to a trade vertical lead generation shop whose proof is growth, not cases: the headline claim is two Inc. 5000 listings, 2025 and 2026.

The menu is the trades multiplied by two channels: Roofing Marketing, Roofing SEO, Roofing PPC, HVAC Marketing, HVAC SEO, Plumbing Marketing, Plumbing SEO, Remodeling SEO, Construction Company Marketing, Storage Company Marketing and PPC Services. Three capabilities score 2 and form the core with no lead line: SEO (trade SEO services per prior search; a 944 URL blog with 200 updated in a year), Paid Search (Roofing PPC and PPC services; 32 own Google ads, 15 in the last 30 days) and AI Search / GEO (12 blog URLs on AI search, GEO and AEO, including AEO for home services and tracking AI rankings). Web & Product scores 1; every other capability, including Local, scores 0; breadth is 4. The record lists no proprietary products, no partners and no CMS, because the homepage capture was unreadable; the blog was updated through April 2026 and confidence in the record is low.

AI posture: content, not product. It publishes heavily on AI search for contractors, but no named AI service or tool was captured, and Horus scores P1 partial for that reason. Moves: 2025, the Inc. 5000 listing; 2026, listed again. No news items, case study text or job postings are on record, and the blog includes rankings of rival home services agencies.

Pricing: the record holds no pricing signal; P5 unknown. Conspicuously absent for a home services lead generation agency: a local line (Local scores 0, and Horus marks P3 not applicable even though the client type is local), any data or measurement line, any CRM or owned audience line, a founding year, a headcount and a pricing page.
clients:
The record describes a local client type, a Minneapolis home market with one office, and six verticals: Roofing, HVAC, Plumbing, Remodeling, Construction and Storage companies. The book is 4 clients, all from blog case study URLs, all names only, observed 0: Aquarius Home Services, Distinctive Roofing, Monarch Roofing and Northface Construction, each with a case study slug and no captured title or text.

The need for each is therefore inferred from the mix Hook Agency leads with: local and lead generation through organic demand and paid performance, since the menu pairs every trade with SEO and PPC and the positioning line says lead generation. The client names support the vertical read, two roofers, a construction firm and a home services company, but nothing in the record says what any of them bought. No client sits on another tracked agency's book (shared_n 0), and no press release names an agency of record.

What the base needs next, read against KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation): contractors that bought rankings and PPC leads are likely, at low confidence, to ask for AI answer visibility next, and Hook Agency has published the content to answer that but shows no audited product, so the ask is open. Read against KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer), the paid search hours those contractors buy are the hours the platforms absorb, and with displacement read at 81.0 and the local ICP adding 12 to the Monsoon index, the base is very likely to buy on price when a cheaper delivered offer arrives; that is a judgment on the mix and the read, not on any named client.

openings:
The strongest opening is price. Monsoon reads Landfall at 75.0 with displacement at 81.0, SEO (26) and Paid Search (17) the most movable hours, and no public pricing model (P5 unknown). An offshore delivered rival pricing trade SEO and PPC line by line in public is very likely, at moderate confidence, to take contractors from a book of 4 undescribed names; the falsifier is a published price on hookagency.com, which the unreadable homepage may already carry.

The product opening is AI content without the product: 12 blog URLs on GEO and AEO and no audited AI visibility number (P1 partial), so a rival with a tracked citation share for a roofer leads with the number. The exposure to press is KJ4: paid search hours with no first party data or measurement depth (P4 partial), no assistant ad testing (P8 absent), no feed, schema or entity work (P2 absent). The local line is the gap: a contractor agency whose Local capability scores 0 leaves LSAs and Sponsored Places, the P3 move, unclaimed. The house is not the opening, its own ads run, though 0 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days says the content engine behind its AI search pitch has stopped.
